clue.text: Plant for the southern border

parts.note: an edge is a border or margin

explanation.surface: A gardener chooses something to grow along the south side of the flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern border' reads as a garden bed, but it splits into S for southern and EDGE for border.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedges are grass-like waterside plants of the genus Carex.

clue.text: The end of Hassan's golden journey

definitions.text: The end of Hassan's golden journey

parts.words: The end of Hassan's golden journey
parts.note: James Elroy Flecker's play Hassan closes with the poem The Golden Journey, whose destination city in Uzbekistan is named in its title

explanation.walkthrough: Flecker's verse play Hassan (1922) ends with pilgrims setting out on 'The Golden Journey to Samarkand'; the city is that journey's goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Samarkand, the Silk Road city in Uzbekistan, is the destination in Flecker's poem title.

clue.text: Carriage of Alice's cat, say ?

indicators.note: say tells us the cat's name is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's Alice books, Alice's cat is called Dinah

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what vehicle Alice's pet might ride in.
explanation.walkthrough: Dinah, Alice's cat in Carroll's books, said out loud gives DINER, a railway dining car.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is a railway carriage where meals are served, a dining car.

clue.text: Sloth, perhaps, displayed in garden and gallery

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A lazy creature is on show in a garden and an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the sin of laziness; here it is the animal. The Tate is a major London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentates are toothless mammals of an old zoological order that includes sloths, anteaters and armadillos.

clue.text: Instrument sent back by no dull crowd

indicators.note: sent back tells us the whole run of words that follows is to be read in reverse order, letters too

parts.note: drab means dull or dreary
a mob is a crowd

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is returned because a lively audience didn't want it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the whole string NODRABMOB end to end, giving BOM + BARD + ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardon is a bass tuba-like brass instrument used in military bands.

clue.text: What a dull-sounding creature!

indicators.note: sounding asks for a word with the same sound as the one meaning dull

parts.note: a bore is something dull and tedious

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how boring some animal is.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore is a dull thing; the same sound spelt differently is the wild pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig or uncastrated male pig, an animal.

clue.text: Like one's length, if liable to be floored

definitions.text: Like one's length, if liable to be floored

parts.words: Like one's length, if liable to be floored
parts.note: to measure one's length is an idiom for falling flat on the ground; something that can be measured fits the length that is liable to be floored

explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure one's length' is an old idiom for falling flat; a length that can be laid out on the floor that way is fit to be measured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of being sized up or quantified is able to be measured.

clue.text: Rising island artist, fit for cultivation

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read from the bottom up, so the run of words is reversed

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming island painter whose land is good for farming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses ELBARA as a whole, giving ARABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is ground suited to ploughing and growing crops.

clue.text: Unload Bud's 2 for a change

indicators.note: for a change says the letters are to be altered into a new order

parts.note: the name Bud plus its S, taken as written
2 refers to the answer at 2 Down, a railway dining car

explanation.surface: Telling someone called Bud to unload, with a cross-reference thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is BUDS plus DINER, the answer to 2 Down, rearranged into DISBURDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To disburden is to relieve of a load, to unburden.

clue.text: Nick is no companion

parts.note: no can mean not, as in 'no better'
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A man called Nick is said to be a poor friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it means a small cut. CH is Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or indentation, the same as a notch.

clue.text: A giggle, we hear, from a Dacotah maiden ?

definitions.text: A giggle, we hear, from a Dacotah maiden

parts.words: A giggle, we hear, from a Dacotah maiden
parts.note: the heroine of Longfellow's Hiawatha is a Dakota girl whose name means laughing water, and it sounds like a girl's name followed by 'ha ha'

explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow's The Song of Hiawatha gives the Dakota maiden a name meaning 'laughing water'; spoken, it sounds like Minnie plus a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnehaha is the Dakota heroine of Longfellow's poem The Song of Hiawatha.

clue.text: Advantage of a girl's return

indicators.note: return says the girl's name is turned back to front

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Asking what benefit a girl gets when she comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses TESSA.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, a benefit.

clue.text: It isn't common, so beam about the right to have it

indicators.note: about tells us the beam goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A muddled reasoning about light and entitlement to own something special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R and IT inside RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something uncommon or seldom found.

clue.text: Leave the ermine by the Irish lake

parts.note: ermine is a prized white fur
lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: Instructions to abandon an ermine coat beside a lake in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' reads as a verb; it is the noun, time off. LOUGH is the Irish lake word.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlough is a leave of absence, especially for soldiers.

clue.text: His type is all set to provide information

definitions.text: His type is all set to provide information

parts.words: His type is all set to provide information
parts.note: the man in question arranges printing type so that pages of text can be printed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like 'his sort of person'; it is printing type, which this worker sets by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor sets type for printing.

clue.text: Supplementary aid to lad in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble, read with the fodder, says these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Extra help is given to a boy who has got into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' signals the anagram of AIDTOLADIN; the 'in' before it is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementary means added or extra.

clue.text: Cease to live with the artist -he arranges courses

parts.note: to die is to cease to live
Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to die alongside a painter, set against a man arranging something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' looks like educational courses but means courses of a meal, which a nutrition expert plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition expert plans meals and diets, arranging what courses are eaten.

clue.text: Backs the prevailing fashion in Esau's country

indicators.note: backs here means turns backwards, so the fashion word is reversed

parts.note: the mode is the prevailing fashion

explanation.surface: Someone supports the latest trend in a biblical land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' looks like 'supports'; it reverses MODE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau founded the Edomites, and his land was called by their name.

clue.text: Suspects that watery vapour corrodes

parts.note: mist is watery vapour in the air
rusts means corrodes

explanation.surface: Someone suspects that damp air is rotting the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to doubt or distrust them.

clue.text: The setting being America ?

parts.note: the setting is where the sun sets, the West, and America lies in the western world

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' reads as a story's location; it is the sun setting, in the West, with America as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is the West, the region of the sunset, which includes the Americas.

clue.text: Fight for what is owed to many

parts.note: a due is what is owed
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, crossword shorthand for many

explanation.surface: Arguing over what is owed to a crowd of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people.

clue.text: They are anxious not to miss the post

definitions.text: They are anxious not to miss the post

parts.words: They are anxious not to miss the post
parts.note: these people are eager not to miss out on a job, the post, rather than the mail

explanation.walkthrough: 'The post' looks like the mail; it is a job vacancy they hope to get.
explanation.definitionFit: Job seekers putting in for a position hope to be offered the post.

clue.text: Agree to request of Bill Grant

parts.note: AC (account) is a bill
to cede is to grant or yield

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill Grant is being asked to agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Grant' looks like a name; it splits into AC (account) and CEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede is to consent to a request or demand.

clue.text: Royal personage incorporated briefly in the crowd

indicators.note: in says the short form goes inside the crowd

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd
Inc is the short form of incorporated

explanation.surface: A royal joins a crush of people in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts INC inside PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family.

clue.text: Carthaginian constable takes in a French one

indicators.note: takes in tells us the constable holds the French word inside

parts.note: PC is police constable
un is French for a
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A police officer brings in a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' puts UN and I inside PC.
explanation.definitionFit: Punic means relating to ancient Carthage, as in the Punic Wars.

clue.text: Healthier mechanic

definitions.meaning: a workman who fits and assembles machine parts

explanation.definitionFit: Fitter means in better shape, and a fitter is a mechanic who assembles or adjusts machinery.

clue.text: A journey to the east? Nonsense !

parts.note: a trip is a journey
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Scoffing at the idea of a journey eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins TRIP and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is rubbish talk, from the cheap offal.

clue.text: Lorelei's song for, example was deceptive

definitions.meaning: a German song, such as the setting of Heine's poem about the Rhine siren

explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'for' is an OCR slip for 'song, for example'. Lied is the German word for song.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German art song, such as Heine's Lorelei set to music, and lied means told untruths.

clue.text: Sound like a poet ?

indicators.note: like asks for a word sounding the same as the poet's name

parts.note: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, author of The Highwayman

explanation.surface: A question about what a poet's voice sounds like.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes, author of 'The Highwayman', has a name pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is a sound, often a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: Old tile-yards by the Louvre

parts.note: the Paris palace gardens beside the Louvre took their name from the tile kilns that once stood there

explanation.walkthrough: The Paris gardens next to the Louvre are named after the tile works (French tuiles, tiles) on the site.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuileries palace and gardens in Paris stand on the site of former tile kilns.

clue.text: Compare the colour granted

parts.note: confer, abbreviated cf., is Latin for compare
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to compare shades of paint before granting approval.
explanation.walkthrough: CONFER means 'compare'; it is the Latin word behind the abbreviation cf.
explanation.definitionFit: Conferred means bestowed or awarded, as an honour is granted.

clue.text: They bowed themselves when Orpheus sang

definitions.text: They bowed themselves when Orpheus sang

parts.words: They bowed themselves when Orpheus sang
parts.note: Shakespeare's song in Henry VIII begins 'Orpheus with his lute made' woodland things and mountain tops bow

explanation.walkthrough: From Henry VIII: 'Orpheus with his lute made trees, And the mountain tops that freeze, Bow themselves when he did sing.'
explanation.definitionFit: In the Shakespeare song, Orpheus's music makes the woods and peaks bend to listen.
